_comment: Public footage bundles. Every machine downloads the same bytes from a permanent URL and
checks the sha256 before using them, so a run on real footage is reproducible without
anybody having to ship a video file — which is what the generated fixture existed to work
around, and what a personal recording could never offer.
Why Wikimedia: upload.wikimedia.org URLs are permanent and content-addressed by path, the
licence of every file is machine-readable, and nothing behind them expires or rotates.
Stock libraries were rejected: Pexels and Pixabay read as CC0 but forbid redistributing
content 'on a Standalone basis', and their URLs are not stable.

Codec note: the LGPL ffmpeg this benchmark prefers has no software AV1 decoder — its only av1 entry is hardware-only, and decoding an AV1 Commons file here yields zero frames. Several otherwise ideal 60 fps Commons screencasts are AV1 and therefore unusable. Sources here are VP8/VP9.

Frame rate: sources are chosen at 60 fps native, matching the pinned output. A 25 fps source would leave every app converting the rate inside the interval being timed, and duplicating frames is not the same work as interpolating motion. Of 623 HD videos surveyed on Commons, 263 are >=50 fps and non-AV1, but only 32 are genuine 1920x1080 screen recordings at 60.

commons-upload.description: A Wikimedia Commons upload walked through in a desktop browser, with a webcam-framed presenter track — the shape of a real product demo, recorded at the rate the benchmark exports at.
notes: Neither clip carries cursor telemetry — a downloaded video never does. The pointer track is generated from the fixture seed, so it is identical on every machine but does not follow the cursor visible in the footage.

Both clips are 60 fps at the source, which is the rate the benchmark exports at. Preparation still passes them through ffmpeg -r 60 so the file handed to every app is constant-rate, but no frames are invented or repeated to get there.
The screen clip is trimmed to the first 60 s; the camera clip runs 232 s and is trimmed to the same window.
